source.title: Generalization properties of neural network approximations to frustrated magnet ground states
source.authors: T. Westerhout; N. Astrakhantsev; K. Tikhonov; M. Katsnelson; A. Bagrov

record.file_problem: Full paper and supplemental material supplied.
record.tranche_reason: Tests neural-network generalization on quantum many-body wavefunctions, an additional domain outside the listed claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper trains networks to generalize ground-state signs or amplitudes from sampled Hilbert-space configurations. Its results concern overlap with exact ground states, not the natural-label classification error or the specific measures in V1–V8. Batch-size dependence is mentioned as a training consideration, but no batch-size result is reported.
record.test_reason: The study measures generalization of quantum ground-state signs and amplitudes using wavefunction overlap. None of V1–V8 names this result. Its CNN comparison concerns spin configurations rather than images; its batch-size statement concerns required training-set size rather than held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets. A new domain alone does not establish a test of a listed version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate but omits the central conclusion: for the studied neural quantum states, generalization of signs from small samples, rather than expressibility, is the principal obstacle in frustrated regimes. Amplitudes generalize more easily, and incorporating translational symmetry helps. The authors qualify these findings as heuristic and architecture-dependent.
record.recipe_differences: Supervised learning of exact quantum ground-state wavefunctions from sampled Hilbert-space configurations; uses overlap rather than classification error or train-test error gaps.
record.method_sensitivity: Generalization changes with frustration, training-set fraction, lattice, architecture, and whether the network learns signs or amplitudes. The paper says critical training fraction depends non-monotonically on batch size, but gives no batch-size result.

fits_no_version.finding: Sign generalization deteriorates near frustrated regimes despite high expressibility; amplitude learning is easier, and symmetry-preserving CNNs improve generalization on square and triangular lattices.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Quantum-state generalization depends on frustration, the learned wavefunction component, and architectural symmetry.

fits_no_version.finding: Sign generalization improves abruptly above a training-set-size threshold; the critical sample count grows relatively slowly across the tested square-lattice system sizes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Neural quantum-state sign learning can exhibit a sample-size threshold whose scaling differs from Hilbert-space growth.

fits_no_version.finding: The Methods section states that critical training fraction depends non-monotonically on batch size and that an unsuitable batch size can increase it tenfold.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Batch-size choice can substantially change the sample requirement for quantum-state sign generalization.

record.problems: Most plotted results are figure-only in the supplied text. Results focus on moderately sized exactly diagonalized spin systems and sign/amplitude overlap, so they do not directly establish ordinary natural-label classification generalization.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. The text mentions batch-size dependence on critical εtrain and compares stochastic reconfiguration behavior, but does not report a batch-size result; figures comparing SR are not extracted as they measure optimization accuracy rather than the listed claim versions.

untested.parts: Fixed random-label fitting, natural-label held-out accuracy, and chance-level random-label generalization.
Width-dependent test error beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-classification performance and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD generalization under specified tuning budgets.
Large versus small batches under fixed epoch budgets and recipe changes that reduce any penalty.
Dropout's effect on held-out classification error; mentioning dropout experiments supplies no comparative result.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, train-test gaps, and comparison with norm- or margin-based measures.
Removal of highly memorized examples versus random removal and resulting test accuracy.

record.verdict_notes: No verdicts are warranted for V1–V8. The batch-size statement is an explicit qualitative result, although no batch-size sweep or fixed-epoch comparison is supplied. cannot_determine denotes lack of a measure for a listed version, not lack of evidence for the study's own quantum-state findings.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label held-out classification.
Width sweep beyond the interpolation threshold and test error.
Image-classification comparison of convolutional and fully connected networks.
Adaptive optimizer versus SGD held-out performance.
A reported comparison of batch sizes and held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets.
Dropout intervention and held-out classification error.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its ranking of train-test gaps.
Removal of memorized training examples and resulting test accuracy.

rows.subject: 2-layer dense

rows.operation_detail: Varied Hilbert-space size and measured critical training dataset size for non-zero sign generalization.
rows.measure: Critical training dataset size as a function of Hilbert-space dimension.
rows.value: 36 spins: K ≃ 9·109; training dataset increase by a factor of 10
rows.note: The text says that increasing system size from 24 to 36 spins required increasing the training dataset just by a factor of 10.
rows.check: The Hilbert-space dimensions are system-size conditions, not measured critical training-set sizes. The reported tenfold training-set increase is a valid textual summary, but numerical thresholds are figure-only and should be distinguished by frustration condition. This scaling result tests no listed version.

source_check.correct: For the square lattice, increasing system size from 24 spins (Hilbert-space dimension K ≃ 2.7 × 10^6) to 36 spins (K ≃ 9 × 10^9) requires a tenfold increase in training-set size for nonzero generalization. The K values are system dimensions, not baseline and outcome measurements of critical training-set size. Absolute critical training-set sizes are figure-only.
